cases.reason: A paraphrased explicit-only boundary is valid without a literal Invoke ONLY opener.
A Meta capability summary omits its required explicit-request boundary.
An existing-adoption boundary for an optional tool is legitimate.
An ambient alternative bypasses an otherwise explicit Meta gate.
Approval before a mutation is separate from selecting a Project diagnostic skill.
A Project skill incorrectly requires its exact name despite relevant symptoms.
A quoted automatic-activation mistake is not the operative Meta policy.
Mentioning explicit requests does not help when the description expressly permits ambient activation.
Japanese wording can express the same explicit-only boundary.
A Japanese Meta capability summary still lacks an explicit-request restriction.
The word only can restrict the adopted project environment rather than require a skill-name invocation.
The operative maintenance role is Meta even without relying on the literal word Meta.
An unrelated performance note does not change an explicit-only Meta gate.
The same unrelated performance note does not repair an ambient Meta activation route.
A build note has no skill YAML description or activation policy to judge.
An unrelated unit inconsistency does not establish a description activation-policy defect.
A task-based router loads matching skills and preserves the explicit-request gate of routed Meta skills.
A router description also permits automatic maintenance of installed skills.
An unrelated build note does not change the task-based routing boundary.
